summary: Full-extraction pass over 16 stored documents: the St. Kitts CIU Act 2024, eight St. Kitts audit reports on the public accounts (2016, 2018-2024), two Vanuatu Citizenship Office fee documents and five Vanuatu Treasury December reports. Added the yearly split of CIU revenue by component (government fees, Hurricane Relief Fund, Sustainable Growth Fund, application and background-check fees) for 2018-2024, CBI budget targets for 2015-2016, CBI programme costs and CBI dividend payouts from appropriation warrants, December collections and forecasts for Vanuatu, and the remaining CIIP and DSP fee rows. All component splits add up to the printed totals within rounding.

observations.notes: Federal Government of St. Kitts only (excludes Nevis Island Administration). Budget estimate of Citizenship by Investment fees for 2015 ("this source" = Citizenship by Investment fees, previous sentence). The 2015 outturn is not given in this report.

observations.quote: revenue collected under the Citizenship by Investment programme surpassed its 2016 target of $150 million by $25 million.
observations.notes: Federal Government of St. Kitts only (excludes Nevis Island Administration). 2016 budget target for revenue under the Citizenship by Investment programme; actual 2016 collection by the CIU was $175 million (same report). Also stated on p. 14 ("reduced from $200 million in 2015 to $150 million in 2016").

observations.quote: Citizenship by Investment fees accounted for 92% of the total collections by the Citizenship by Investment Unit. Application fees and due diligence fees accounted for the balance of the revenue collections.

Share of the CIU's 2016 collections ($175 million) that were "Citizenship by Investment fees" (as distinct from application and due diligence fees, which made up the remaining 8%, not split further). Amounts are not printed.

observations.quote: This target was surpassed with $25 million in receipts from the European Union and $15 million from the Sugar Industry Diversification Foundation (SIDF).

Budgetary grant received by the Federal Government from the Sugar Industry Diversification Foundation in 2016, as recorded in the public accounts. events.title: Direct invoicing of agents

events.title: CIU Act published: how CBI money is split
events.description: Citizenship by Investment Unit Act 2024 published (assented 19 June). Sustainable Island State Contributions and other statutory contributions, less agents' fees, go directly to the Consolidated Fund; the Unit keeps application, agent and due diligence fees and a share of post-approval-in-principle fees set by Cabinet, not above 50 percent; financial year July-June; audited accounts to be gazetted and an annual report submitted by 31 October. Comes into force on dates set by ministerial order.
events.quote: which percentage shall not exceed fifty percent;

new_indicators.name: Share of CBI revenue from one component
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of a CBI unit's collections (as recorded in the fiscal accounts) in a period that came from one component (e.g. contributions, application fees, due diligence fees), as stated by the source. Use breakdown category= for the component.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-kna-vut for the St. Kitts 2016 audit report, which gives only a share (92% "Citizenship by Investment fees"). Where amounts are printed, record them as cbi_fiscal_revenue with category= instead.

new_indicators.name: Balance of a CBI-related government account
new_indicators.definition: Balance at a date of a government account or fund held for, or named after, a citizenship- or residence-by-investment programme or its unit (e.g. a CIU deposit or contingency account), as listed in public accounts or by the source. Use breakdown category= for the account.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-kna-vut (St. Kitts 2016 audit report, inactive deposit accounts "CIU Contingency Account" and "Office of the Prime Minister/CIU"). Narrower savings funds keep cbi_contingency_fund_balance.

new_indicators.name: CBI receipts as a share of operating cash receipts
new_indicators.definition: CBI money collected by the government (e.g. CIU fees) divided by total receipts from operating activities in the government cash flow statement, as calculated by the source.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-kna-vut for the St. Kitts audit reports (2018: 32%, 2019: 36%). Different denominator from cbi_fiscal_revenue_pct_revenue (recurrent or total revenue).

new_indicators.name: Government spending on running a CBI programme
new_indicators.definition: Money the government appropriates or spends in a period on operating a citizenship- or residence-by-investment programme (due diligence, consultancy, marketing, unit operating costs), as stated by the source. Status budget for appropriations, actual for spending. Use breakdown category= for the cost type.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-kna-vut for St. Kitts appropriation warrants (2018 consultancy/operations and marketing; 2020-2021 due diligence and operating costs).

new_indicators.name: CBI dividend paid to citizens
new_indicators.definition: Cash payments to a country's citizens or residents financed from, and named after, citizenship-by-investment revenue (e.g. St. Kitts and Nevis "Citizenship by Investment Dividend"), in a period. Status budget for appropriations, actual for recorded spending.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-kna-vut for the St. Kitts audit reports 2022-2023.

ledger.contains: Citizenship by Investment Unit Act, 2024 (No. 11 of 2024), 10 pages: makes the CIU a body corporate with a Board of Governors and senior officers; lists the Unit's funds (first-year appropriation; application, agent and due diligence fees; a share of post-approval-in-principle fees set by Cabinet, not above 50 percent; borrowing); sends Sustainable Island State Contributions and other statutory contributions, less agents' fees, straight to the Consolidated Fund 'as set out in the Second Schedule' (the schedule is not printed in this copy); financial year 1 July-30 June; audited accounts gazetted; annual report by 31 October; fine up to fifty thousand dollars for obstructing the auditor (not a programme number). No statistics, prices or fee amounts. Rules recorded as events: passage on 14 June 2024 (already in the data) and, new, publication on 28 June 2024 with the funding split.

National Audit Office report on the 2016 public accounts of the Federal Government (St. Kitts). Programme content: CIU collected $175 million in 2016 (already recorded) against a $150 million target, down from a $200 million estimate for 2015 (both budgets now recorded); 'Citizenship by Investment fees' were 92% of CIU collections, application and due diligence fees the rest (share recorded; no amounts printed); $15 million budgetary grant from the Sugar Industry Diversification Foundation (recorded as a payment out of a CBI-financed fund); balances of two inactive deposit accounts, 'CIU Contingency Account' and 'Office of the Prime Minister/CIU', at end-2015 and end-2016 (recorded). Year-on-year changes and variances against the revenue projection are printed but not recorded (derived comparisons; the projection itself is not printed). Out of scope: other departments' revenue, taxes, expenditure, debt, deposit accounts and the special audits. Image-only pages (3-5, 7, 9, 39, 45) OCR'd: covers, letter, blanks.

Audit report on the 2018 public accounts. Programme content: CIU collected $418 million (recorded) = government fees $78m + Hurricane Relief Fund $242m + Sustainable Growth Fund $2m + application fees $8m + background checks $88m (components now recorded; they add up to 418); CIU 46% of recurrent revenue (recorded) and 32% of operating cash receipts (recorded); appropriation warrants for CBI consultancy and operating costs in Q4 2018 ($56m) and CIU marketing fees ($14m) (recorded). Year-on-year changes and variances against the revenue projection are printed but not recorded (derived comparisons; the projection itself is not printed). Not recorded: a $10 million warrant for the SIDF (government money paid to the foundation, not CBI receipts). Out of scope: other departments' revenue, taxes, expenditure, debt, deposit accounts and the special audits.
